candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes the TEMPI syndrome pentad: Telangiectasias, Erythrocytosis with elevated Erythropoietin, Monoclonal gammopathy (IgG κ, 910 mg/dL), Perinephric fluid collections, and Intrapulmonary shunting. HHT shares telangiectasias and intrapulmonary shunting but is a hereditary condition caused by mutations in endoglin/ACVRL1, lacks monoclonal protein, perinephric fluid collections, and erythrocytosis with elevated EPO. The candidate correctly identifies intrapulmonary shunting and telangiectasias but assigns an incompatible etiology and diagnostic entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: HHT is a hereditary vascular disorder; TEMPI is an acquired plasma cell dyscrasia syndrome with a distinct pentad

case_quality_flags: Classic TEMPI syndrome case with all five components of the pentad documented; HHT is a common differential but is excluded by the monoclonal protein and perinephric fluid collections
